comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD explicitly identify hyperscale data centers and large public cloud providers as key customers for their data center platforms and products. NVDA discloses that its Compute & Networking segment includes Data Center accelerated computing and networking platforms, which drive the AI infrastructure these customers use. AMD similarly states that hyperscale customers purchase substantial portions of AMD's server CPUs and GPU accelerators to support public cloud services and AI workloads, including generative AI models. The comparison highlights a shared dependency on the same customer segment for high-performance computing hardware, although NVDA focuses on its specific accelerated computing and networking ecosystem while AMD details the broader mix of server CPUs and GPUs supplied to these entities.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

Large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers directly and indirectly purchase a substantial portion of our data center-focused products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SOCs.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.
